description: Pilot worksheets for the eleven FO 1.0 Blue actions, produced by the PLI classification agent strictly executing the trial codebook. Blue's declared Strategic Orientation in FO 1.0: Reframing. Move 1 executes 2026; Move 2 executes 2027. Enriched 2026-07-11 with instrument_of_power and ne_facets for multi-track schema compatibility. Quarterly FO demo: submission_month uses notional 3-month spacing on the locked Blue chronology (demo of quarterly engine for FO 1.0 pack).

classification.rule_citation: Step 1 economic gate: primary mechanism is diplomatic/informational wedge-driving, not an economic instrument - routes to NE

precedent.rationale: Not applicable - non-economic action routed out of macroeconomic adjudication at the Step 1 gate

fit.rationale: Not applicable - non-economic action; Glasl and National Interest tracks adjudicate separately

classification.rule_citation: L2 boundary: technology exclusion from the domestic market by origin is an export-control/entity-exclusion instrument (I2.04), not a trade tariff (L1)

citations: Export Control Reform Act of 2018, 50 U.S.C. 4801 et seq.
Executive Order 13873 (Securing the ICT and Services Supply Chain, 2019)
Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019 (rip-and-replace)
precedent.rationale: Exclusion authorities of this class exist (ICTS, covered-list regimes) but a blanket statutory exclusion of BRICS+ technology has never been exercised at this scope - existing but untested authority

modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Vague statutory definitions require rulemaking before enforcement; effect lags the move horizon

fit.rationale: Coercive market exclusion imposes costs rather than building alternatives - partial contradiction of Reframing

classification.rule_citation: Tie-break rule 8: domestic subsidy / deregulation / procurement routes to L7; permitting deregulation is I7.02

citations: FAST-41, 42 U.S.C. 4370m (permitting acceleration, proven since 2015)
Energy Act of 2020, critical minerals provisions
Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023, NEPA amendments
precedent.rationale: Permitting-reform authority is proven and repeatedly exercised; this action extends a demonstrated instrument class

modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Mine permitting and litigation cycles run longer than the move horizon even after reform
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires synchronized action by Interior, EPA, USDA Forest Service, and the Army Corps

fit.rationale: Domestic capacity-building for critical minerals is a direct Reframing mechanism; environmental friction is secondary

classification.rule_citation: L1 definition: trade-remedy investigation (Section 301/232 class) is I1.03; ICTS review rides as secondary I2.03 per the split-at-intake note

citations: Section 301, Trade Act of 1974, 19 U.S.C. 2411 (exercised against the PRC 2018-2025)
Section 232, Trade Expansion Act of 1962, 19 U.S.C. 1862
USTR Section 301 China Technology Transfer investigation (2017-2018)
precedent.rationale: Deep, repeatedly exercised trade-remedy precedent against the same target; proven authority in the strongest sense

fit.rationale: Executable coercive tool but orientation-agnostic: investigations impose pressure, neither building nor undermining Reframing alternatives

classification.rule_citation: L4 boundary: punitive financial extraction (forced remuneration/asset action) is a financial-coercion instrument I4.06, not a trade remedy

citations: No authority exists to compel retroactive IP remuneration from foreign sovereigns; IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1701) permits blocking, not forced payment
Takings and due-process constraints (U.S. Const. amend. V) bar the proposed seizure mechanism
precedent.rationale: No plausible legal pathway: neither sanctions authority nor court process can compel the remuneration scheme as designed

modifier_rationales.partners_committed: Plurilateral coalition declared in the submission commits partner enforcement, the only executable fragment

fit.rationale: Coercive extraction directly cuts against Reframing's build-alternatives logic

classification.rule_citation: L8 definition: physical reserve acquisition and stockpile expansion is I8.01

citations: Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act, 50 U.S.C. 98 et seq.
Defense Production Act Title III, 50 U.S.C. 4531 (used for minerals and pharma inputs)
National Defense Stockpile Transaction Fund appropriations, FY2024-FY2026 NDAA
precedent.rationale: Standing reserve authority exercised continuously since 1939; direct precedent for both minerals and medical stockpiling

modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Acquisition at stockpile scale runs on multi-year procurement and budget cycles

fit.rationale: Resilience-building reduces dependence without coercion - advances Reframing with only budgetary friction

classification.rule_citation: Tie-break rule 8: domestic subsidy routes to L7 (I7.01); partner regulatory synchronization rides as secondary I9.02

citations: CHIPS and Science Act of 2022, Pub. L. 117-167 (sectoral subsidy authority class)
Bioeconomy EO 14081 (2022) - biomanufacturing initiative without dedicated appropriations
precedent.rationale: The subsidy authority class exists and has been exercised for other sectors, but biotech-specific appropriations of this shape are new - existing but untested for this instrument application

fit.rationale: Sectoral capacity-building subsidy is a core Reframing mechanism; bilateral regulatory sync is supportive

classification.rule_citation: L6 definition: joint purchasing / pooled procurement facility with partners is I6.05

citations: Minerals Security Partnership (2022) - coordination forum, no pooled purchasing authority
No existing US-EU joint procurement facility for minerals; new instrument and appropriations required
precedent.rationale: A plurilateral purchasing facility requires new authority and a negotiated framework that does not exist; allied coordination was never verified before withdrawal

fit.rationale: Coalition-building around alternative supply advances Reframing; unverified partner commitment adds friction

classification.rule_citation: L6 definition: third-country infrastructure finance for telecom buildout is I6.04

citations: BUILD Act of 2018 (DFC) - existing agency but lending capacity far below the initiative's scale
The submission assumes IP-enforcement revenue as the funding source, which does not exist (see M1-A5 Tier 4 finding)
precedent.rationale: The delivery agency exists but the funding mechanism assumed by the plan does not; new appropriations or authority are required to execute at stated scale

modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Infrastructure disbursement and buildout run well past the move horizon; assumed EU co-funding not established

fit.rationale: Building third-country alternatives to PRC telecom infrastructure is textbook Reframing - no contradicting element

classification.rule_citation: Tie-break rule 8: domestic R&D funding routes to L7 (I7.04); standards alignment rides as secondary I9.02

citations: CHIPS and Science Act of 2022, Title I (NSF/DOE research authorizations)
National Quantum Initiative Act of 2018 (research-program authority class)
precedent.rationale: Research-funding authority of this class exists and is exercised; the bundled multi-domain program at this scope is untested and its Great Firewall ambitions dilute instrument clarity

fit.rationale: Research capacity-building advances Reframing; bundled information-control ambitions are neutral-to-mixed secondaries

classification.rule_citation: L4 boundary: secondary sanctions on third-party transactions are I4.02; mineral import thresholds ride as secondary I1.04

citations: IEEPA, 50 U.S.C. 1701 (blocking authority, repeatedly exercised)
CAATSA (2017) secondary-sanctions framework - exercised against Russia/Iran, never at commodity-threshold scope against PRC minerals
precedent.rationale: Secondary-sanctions authority exists and is exercised, but the commodity-threshold trigger at this scope is untested against this target

fit.rationale: Broad coercive escalation under a declared Reframing orientation - primary mechanism cuts against building alternatives
